summary: Reverse the sequence: obtain the developer’s current requirement, use the tailored search brief, validate one specific offering, then test affordable transferable control. This is a research and call-priority dataset; no new site has passed investment or control gates.

methodology.event: The modeled event is that the named developer funds and begins physical construction of a first permanent data-center phase, or a major incremental conversion/expansion, on the identified offering by October 29, 2031. A purchase, announcement, land clearing or existing facility operation alone does not count. Actual buyer-specific construction probability is not yet estimable from public evidence.
assumptions: User-specified condition: adequate technically deliverable power capacity for the buyer-approved first phase is demonstrated. None of these sites currently has utility-verified available MW in this research. Facility MW and critical IT MW are kept distinct; no fixed PUE conversion is assumed.

Power suitability does not silently waive power price, upgrade allocation, collateral, tariff, redundancy, exact service date or transferability. Those commercial and scheduling issues remain in the execution gates unless the buyer separately accepts them.

Each numerical scenario shows three subjective conditional inputs: buyer selection given power × non-power feasibility given selection × financed construction start given preceding gates. This is a conditional chain, not multiplication of independent marginal risks.

Low/base/high outputs are products of the displayed assumption inputs, rounded to whole percentages. They are transparent planning cases, not measured rates, confidence intervals or statistically calibrated forecasts. You can change the base inputs in the site card to see sensitivity.

The first-phase load in each card is a hypothesis to validate with the buyer. It is not an available-MW claim, engineering design or developer mandate. All other information is held at the public-evidence stage.

Buyer identity, customers, competing owned inventory, customer latency, layout, permits, cooling/water, fiber construction, funding, seller cooperation and economics remain material. Existing facilities are modeled only for incremental build or major conversion.

Hinds, the unavailable TRIC listing and the auction adjacency hypothesis receive no numerical scenario until their stated status/identity gates are resolved. Archived or rejected leads do not acquire a forecast merely because power is assumed.
limitations: 100 profiles are not 100 confirmed buyers. The directory includes operating developers, owner-builders, powered-land/master developers and nine international watch profiles. Roles and parent/JV links are disclosed.

No developer has reviewed these site matches. Sources include published intake criteria, regulatory filings, project announcements, company pages and broker/EDC offerings. Project precedents are not universal purchasing requirements.

No negative-project denominator, comparable conversion cohort or private buying mandate exists in this dataset. These subjective ranges can be substantially wrong; they must not be used as a land valuation or justification for spending.

A buyer may build yet never buy a Syncranicity option. Sale price is not option cost. Assignment rights, seller authority, utility study reliance/transfer and compensation have not been established for any new lead.

Matches share risks and some companies share parents or JVs. Do not add the percentages or calculate an at-least-one-buyer probability as if the opportunities were independent. Site counts are marketed offering records: the older Ovilla Road and Project Venus records may overlap and are flagged for parcel reconciliation.

Availability, asking prices and published plans can change. A listing or EDC record is evidence of marketing, not seller confirmation. APNs shown are reported identifiers, not a title or boundary certification.
The existing <$100,000 founder capital constraint, $5,000 learning cap and $10,000 soft-control cap remain unchanged. This research authorizes no payment, bid, reservation or outreach.

actions.title: Validate three different buying briefs
actions.why: Start with metrobloks, Dataprana and AIB because their different published products can reject whole categories of land before spending.
actions.script: I source conditional land and utility-rights opportunities. Before sending a parcel, I want to confirm the exact market, first-phase MW, latest service date and transaction you would consider. Your published criteria suggest a particular search lane; is it active today?
actions.voicemail: I am validating your current land-acquisition brief before submitting sites. Could the person responsible for site selection confirm active metros, phase size and evidence needed for an initial review?
questions: Which markets and first/ultimate MW are open now, and are those facility or critical IT MW?
metrobloks: qualifying IXP/distance method, net acres, FAR and height? Dataprana: accepted ISO/utility territories and 10–50 MW ramp? AIB: actual 40–90 MW minimum and any smaller-phase exception?
What customer commitment, power documents, fiber evidence and entitlement stage are required?
Would you take an assignable contract, direct purchase, landowner JV or staged closing, and who pays for studies/collateral?
actions.success: A named authorized reviewer, written brief, minimum submission package and next review date.
actions.stop: No active geography/product mandate or no acceptable route for a small originator.

actions.title: Test RadiusDC’s Denver expansion gap
actions.why: The Thornton offering advertises dark fiber to RadiusDC’s fully leased 1500 Champa hub. This connects a site feature to a disclosed expansion search, although no parcel interest is verified.
actions.script: Your Denver page says you are evaluating expansion. Would an existing Thornton facility with verified diverse dark-fiber rights to 1500 Champa and a roughly 7 MW facility service envelope fit that requirement? We would first validate actual vacant capacity, rights and conversion economics.
actions.voicemail: I am checking a Champa-connected Thornton facility against your published Denver expansion need. Could your acquisitions or development lead confirm whether this location, scale and acquisition/retrofit structure are relevant?
questions: Is the current need another carrier hub, a connected satellite, or larger purpose-built capacity?
Does Thornton work for the actual customer latency and interconnection product?
What minimum incremental IT capacity, coolant density, vacant-possession and service date are required?
Will you review a broker-led acquisition packet before we pursue any control or paid studies?
actions.success: A named buyer reviewer accepts the specific product/location and states the minimum engineering and commercial evidence.
actions.stop: Wrong scale/product, existing pipeline already covers demand, unusable fiber rights, or tenant encumbrances prevent meaningful expansion.

actions.title: Reconcile Hinds before forecasting it
actions.why: Current pages conflict on status and price; the exact 110-acre carve-out and service territory remain unresolved.
actions.script: Please confirm whether MLS 21317653 is available, the current price, exact county account and survey/legal description for the offered 110 acres. If it is available, would the owner authorize parcel-specific utility diligence and consider an assignable agreement with utility and buyer contingencies?
actions.voicemail: I need to reconcile the current Hinds offering before any further diligence: availability, exact tract, asking price and whether conditional control is possible. Please send the current offering package.
questions: Which current owner/entity has authority and what exact land is offered?
What explains the active/sold and $319k/$352k/$385k differences?
Which utility is authorized to respond for this tract, and can the existing AEP contact document the service path?
What diligence, assignment, deposit and extension terms would the seller actually consider?
actions.success: One reconciled current offering and a written utility-intake path; then validate Dataprana/AIB phase fit.
actions.stop: Unavailable tract, unresolved owner authority or hard-money terms outside existing caps.

actions.title: One Newberry buyer/EDC sprint
actions.why: Compare Dickert and I-26 Public Works only after DC BLOX or DartPoints identifies a real network/customer gap. Old per-acre marketing needs refresh.
actions.script: We are checking whether a small phased data-center opportunity serves a specific regional buyer need. Could you confirm current availability, exact parcels, owners, per-acre pricing and whether a roughly 20-acre initial tract with expansion rights is possible?
actions.voicemail: I am comparing two Newberry industrial offerings against a buyer-specific phased-load requirement. Please send current parcel, pricing, utility and carrier information and the right development contact.
questions: Is there an unmet DC BLOX/DartPoints customer or network need here?
Are Dickert and I-26 still offered, and what subdivisions/expansion rights are permitted?
Who at the cooperative will provide a parcel/load/date-specific written response?
Can two physically diverse carrier routes be built and at what order-of-magnitude cost?
actions.success: A specific buyer reason to locate here plus refreshed owner/parcel and utility/carrier intake data.
actions.stop: Existing regional capacity already serves demand, or network/buildable-area constraints defeat the phase.

actions.title: Test Rocket’s advertised documents
actions.why: Its advertised 50 MW path is a concrete document request. DataBank/CyrusOne should define the required Houston product before paid studies.
actions.script: Your offering references a CenterPoint-studied 50 MW path and expansion. Please provide the exact parcels, current availability, executed or draft utility documents, conditions, service dates and reliance/transfer rights. We are checking a named metro-capacity buyer fit before committing capital.
actions.voicemail: I would like the documents behind Project Rocket’s advertised power path, exact offered acreage and current pricing/contingency terms for a buyer-led review.
questions: What is executed versus studied, and what expires or requires collateral?
Is the first 50 MW facility or IT capacity, and what is the actual deliverability date?
Can a new buyer rely on/assume the studies, service agreements and land rights?
What are the exact fiber routes, flood/drainage findings and current permit requirements?
actions.success: A reviewable utility/land package and a developer willing to compare it with owned Houston alternatives.
actions.stop: No transferable advantage, unclear offering perimeter or unaffordable hard control.

actions.title: Use Rural Hall to shape diligence with a buyer
actions.why: Seller-funded study underway and a request for early buyer input make this a direct test of the buyer-first process.
actions.script: The listing says the load study is funded and you welcome early buyer input. Could we align the study/site plan with a specific 40–90 MW developer brief, and clarify the rezoning process, exact parcels and control/assignment route?
actions.voicemail: I am assessing whether a named developer’s phase requirements can inform the existing Rural Hall study. Please share study scope/timing, current entitlement docket and seller’s preferred transaction.
questions: Which utility, applicant and phase are in the existing study?
What is the rezoning docket, current status and realistic decision path?
Can the eventual developer rely on or assume the study and service rights?
What asking price and conditional structure would the owner discuss?
actions.success: AIB or another suitable buyer confirms this market/phase and is willing to guide the next study step.
actions.stop: Buyer needs a different market/product or study/land rights cannot be made usable.

actions.title: Qualify a conversion rather than raw land
actions.why: TECfusions and Patmos have reuse precedents; the Mishawaka shell only helps if conversion beats new construction on cost and schedule.
actions.script: Please provide vacant-possession status, current equipment schedule, environmental reports, structural loading and transferable utility agreements. We are checking phased data-center conversion with a specialist buyer.
actions.voicemail: I am evaluating the former AM General property for a buyer-led technical conversion review. Please send the current sale/lease package, power-service documents and environmental/structural diligence.
questions: What remains from the former electrical system and what is actually serviceable?
Are former peak demand and prospective 50 MW claims supported by current utility documents?
What contamination, roof/floor, cooling-yard, generator/noise and fire constraints exist?
Will the owner consider buyer-backed exclusivity while a specialist screens conversion economics?
actions.success: A specialist developer accepts the market and confirms a reusable technical/cost advantage.
actions.stop: Retrofit scope removes the time/cost benefit or environmental liabilities cannot be allocated.
